title: Campus parking tickets

authoring.author: Parikshaa content team
authoring.originality: Written for Parikshaa: our own project brief, code, tests and rubric for campus parking tickets, examples, code, quiz and explanations; no text from any site, book or course.

brief: The college gate runs a small parking lot for bikes and cars. Build its ticket logic: park a vehicle if a slot of its kind is free, charge it when it leaves (the first 15 minutes are free, then every started hour costs ₹10 for a bike and ₹20 for a car), and report the free slots.
requirements: SLOTS sets up the lot; every other command needs a lot first.
A plate can be parked once at a time; a slot must be free for its type.
Leaving charges 0 for up to 15 minutes, otherwise every started hour at ₹10 (bike) or ₹20 (car).
Times are HH:MM on one day; a leave time before the park time is refused.
io_protocol:
| Command | Prints |
|---|---|
| `SLOTS <bikes> <cars>` | `lot ready: <b> bike, <c> car slots` |
| `PARK <plate> <BIKE or CAR> <HH:MM>` | `ticket <n> for <plate>`, `error: <plate> is already parked`, or `error: no <bike or car> slot free` |
| `LEAVE <plate> <HH:MM>` | `<plate> paid <fee>`, `error: <plate> is not parked`, or `error: time goes backwards` |
| `FREE` | `free: <b> bike, <c> car` |

Tickets are numbered from 1. Anything else: `error: bad command <line>`; a command before SLOTS: `error: no lot yet`.

milestones.title: Parking
milestones.instructions: Fill in `park`: refuse a plate that is already inside, refuse when no slot of that type is free, otherwise take a slot and issue the next ticket.
hints: Check the plate before the slots, so a duplicate gets the duplicate message even when the lot is full.

milestones.title: Leaving and fees
milestones.instructions: Fill in `fee` and `leave`. Every *started* hour is charged: 61 minutes is 2 hours.
hints: Give the slot back only after all checks pass.

rubric.criterion: Hidden tests pass: every command prints exactly the expected output.
ParkingLot owns all slot counts and tickets; the fee rule lives in one static method; no public fields.
Readable names, small functions and clear error handling (AI feedback, advice only).
